title: Ephemeral broker keyflow and SIEM ingest guide
content:
Purpose:
This note documents a compact, operationally pragmatic approach for using ephemeral broker keys with our envelope-encryption topology, mapping key lifecycle events into the RBAC v2 model, and producing SIEM-friendly audit records for evidence automation. It is intended for security engineers, infra SREs, and compliance reviewers who run or certify Redwood private and dedicated deployments.

Scope and goals:
- Define an ephemeral broker key pattern that limits long-lived key material exposure while preserving low-latency decryption for inference workloads.
- Specify an audit log schema for KMS/HSM events that maps cleanly to RBAC v2 roles and SIEM fields.
- Provide playbooks for scheduled rotations, emergency rekey, and BYOK/HSM import with attestation artifacts.
- Outline evidence automation hooks and retention requirements for compliance audits.

Key concepts (quick):
- Root KEK (HSM-wrapped or cloud KMS-stored): very limited use; only rewraps tenant KEKs and issues attestation tokens.
- Tenant KEK: long-lived logical key per tenant used to unwrap envelope keys; may be BYOK-managed for enterprise customers.
- Ephemeral broker keys (EBKs): short-lived symmetric keys generated by broker processes to decrypt cached envelope keys for a bounded time window (minutes-hours). EBKs never leave the broker in plaintext and are rotated frequently.
- Envelope keys (CEKs): used to encrypt data-at-rest; encrypted under Tenant KEK and cached in encrypted form.

Architecture pattern (high level):
1) Data is encrypted with CEK. CEK is encrypted under Tenant KEK and stored with metadata (key_id, wrap_alg, created_at, tenant_id).
2) Broker process requests ephemeral EBK from local KMS proxy. Request is authenticated by RBAC v2 token with scope: broker:issue_ebk for given tenant.
3) KMS proxy generates EBK inside HSM enclave or uses cloud KMS symmetric key to derive ephemeral material that is exported as an encrypted envelope keyed to the broker instance. Plaintext EBK is provided only over an authenticated mTLS channel and held in-process.
4) Broker unwraps CEK with Tenant KEK (via KMS) while EBK is available, rewraps CEK under EBK for fast subsequent decrypts, stores EBK-wrapped CEK in cache with TTL and audit record.
5) EBK TTL enforces short window for cached plaintext exposure; when EBK expires broker must reacquire and rewrap.

RBAC v2 mapping (operations -> roles):
- kms:create_tenant_kek -> role: security-kms-admin (token-scoped to org)
- kms:import_byok -> role: security-onboard-engineer + requiring mfa and approval action
- kms:issue_ebk -> role: broker-service-account (limited to tenant_id and host_group)
- kms:rekey_tenant -> role: platform-ops (can invoke scheduled rekey workflows only)
- kms:emergency_revoke -> role: sec-pager-duty (requires human approval via incident runbook)
Notes: every action recorded in audit and linked to the issuing principal and role_evidence claim. RBAC tokens must carry role_version and request_purpose fields to simplify later evidence queries.

Audit log schema for KMS/HSM events (recommended fields):
- schema_version (string)
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- event_id (UUID)
- request_id (opaque from frontend)
- correlation_id (application trace id)
- actor_id (service account or user id)
- actor_role (RBACv2 role name)
- actor_origin (ip or instance id)
- tenant_id
- action (create_tenant_kek, import_byok, issue_ebk, wrap, unwrap, rotate, retire, revoke)
- resource_key_id (logical id: tenant_kek:<id> or ebk:<id> or cek:<id>)
- key_type (root_kek|tenant_kek|ebk|cek)
- algorithm (AES-GCM, RSA-OAEP, etc.)
- key_version
- key_state (active|pending_rotation|retired|compromised)
- operation_result (success|failure)
- error_code (if failure)
- hsm_slot (if HSM-bound)
- kms_backend (cloud-kms|hsm-cluster-1|local-softkms)
- rotation_policy (manual|scheduled|on_demand)
- rotation_reason (security_review|age|compromise|customer_request)
- attached_evidence (list of artifact ids)
- retention_class (default|sensitive|evidence)

Important SIEM mapping notes:
- Normalize field names to the SIEM canonical schema (use event_id, actor, action, outcome). Provide vendor mappings for Splunk, Elastic, and Sumo.
- Send structured JSON events over a buffered Kafka topic with schema registry; SIEM connectors pull from Kafka and perform final enrichments. Avoid sending free-form logs to cloud audit sinks.
- Use a dedicated topic per environment (prod/dedicated/private) and per retention class.
- Include schema_version on every message to support rolling changes and back-compat.
- Sample event (single-line JSON for SIEM):
{"schema_version":"kms.v1","timestamp":"2026-03-10T14:21:09Z","event_id":"b6b9e8a8-4f3c-4b2b-9f77-7a6d2c0f3e81","request_id":"req-54221","correlation_id":"trace-8f1a","actor_id":"svc-broker-22","actor_role":"broker-service-account","actor_origin":"i-0a1b2c3d","tenant_id":"tenant-42","action":"issue_ebk","resource_key_id":"ebk-0x7a3f","key_type":"ebk","algorithm":"AES-256-GCM","key_version":"v1","key_state":"active","operation_result":"success","kms_backend":"hsm-cluster-1","hsm_slot":"slot-23","rotation_policy":"scheduled","attached_evidence":["attest-20260310-23"],"retention_class":"evidence"} 

Evidence automation and retention:
- For each rotation/important key action generate a compact evidence bundle: { attestation_token, wrapping_proof_hash, action_log_id, approver_id, signed_timestamp }. Store bundles in an immutable evidence bucket (GCS/Azure blob with object versioning + WORM/retention lock) and index pointers into the SIEM event attached_evidence array.
- Evidence bundles should contain HSM attestations where applicable (signed by HSM attestation key), and the KMS operation digest signed by the platform's signing key.
- Retention windows: default 7y for evidence class (subject to legal review), 90d for operational logs. Evidence bucket has stricter access via RBAC v2 and requires 2-person review to remove.

Rotation procedures (concise playbooks):
A) Scheduled tenant KEK rotation (non-emergency):
  1. Open rotation plan in Jira and link ticket to confluence runbook.
  2. Create new tenant KEK via HSM-proxy (kms:create_tenant_kek) with rotation_policy=scheduled and mark old key pending_rotation.
  3. Generate rewrap job that fetches CEK metadata and rewraps CEKs under new tenant KEK. Prefer lazy rewrap for large datasets: tag objects with rewrap_needed and perform background rewrap on next write/read.
  4. Run canary on subset (1% of traffic) for 24 hours; verify audit records and throughput.
  5. Promote new KEK to active, retire old KEK to retired state and set retirement_date. Archive evidence bundle.

B) Emergency compromise (incident):
  1. Trigger incident: create incident ticket and request kms:emergency_revoke. Role: sec-pager-duty must approve.
  2. Revoke affected KEK (immediate), issue new KEK using HSM root with attestation.
  3. Force rewrap on all CEKs; if immediate rewrap impossible use short-lived EBK to decrypt on demand and rewrap; mark objects compromised and notify customers per policy.
  4. Collate evidence bundle (HSM audit logs, rotation evidence, approvals) and ingest into SIEM with high-priority tag.

BYOK / HSM import checklist (minimum):
- Customer provides key import package and attestation cert.
- Validate attestation against approved CAs and device firmware list.
- Import into quarantine HSM slot and create tenant_kek resource pointing at slot id.
- Run attestation verification and generate evidence token.
- Map customer owner to a BYOK-owner RBAC role; create an access policy (no direct export, allowed wrap/unwrap only via KMS API).

Operational notes and gotchas:
- Never export EBK plaintext to persistent storage. If broker crash occurs, EBKs must be considered lost; cache invalidation and forced re-acquisition are required.
- Schema changes must follow a two-phase process: publish new schema_version and run concurrent enrichment in the SIEM until all pipelines accept it.
- Watch for high cardinality fields (actor_origin, instance id) in the SIEM. Use bucketing and sampled indexing for low-value high-cardinality fields.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Confirm retention window for evidence_class with legal for EU customers (GDPR implications for long-term evidence storage).
- Define exact attestation token format for HSM vendors (YubiHSM vs AWS CloudHSM differences).
- Implement automated rewrap job operator (k8s cron + priority queue) and link to this doc.

Appendix: quick references
- Jira runbook template: jira:SEC-ROTATE-TEMPLATE-2025
- Confluence root runbook: confluence:SEC-KMS-OPERATIONS
- Example Github rewrap job: github:redwood-infra/kms-rewrap#branch-ephemeral-broker

Owner and contact: Asha Patel (security-engineering). For urgent incidents call sec-pager-duty.

This doc is intentionally concise; expand sections into separate runbooks when preparing for an authority audit or for onboarding an enterprise BYOK customer.
